variance.question: when the same model runs the same sealed, already-graded brief repeatedly, how much does its score move?
variance.design: K=5 repeats per lane of the sealed T447 brief (byte-identical wrapped prompt, sha256 84ec2845...), fresh --no-session contexts per repeat, frozen fixture worktree at 111c141 (the tree the key answers). Same grader model (claude-opus-5, G3-clean for both lanes) for all repeats of a lane; blind grading of anonymized repeats.
variance.honest_read: DeepSeek-v4-flash's within-model noise floor on this sealed brief is sd ≈ 6.2, range 15 (scores 22–37) on a 30-point rubric, measured blind by the same grader model (claude-opus-5) who scored the original T447 lane. Every adjacent gap in the T-A matrix smaller than ~1 sd is below this lane's own noise: flash(38)–pro(34)=4, pro(34)–glm(30)=4, glm(30)–minimax(27)=3, minimax(27)–sonnet(26)=1 and sonnet(26)–kimi(25)=1 are all unrankable as written; the only robust readings are opus(46) above the field and haiku(0) below it, each >2 sd from the pack. Worse for the ladder: the original n=1 flash score of 38 sits at the top of this lane's own repeat distribution (max 37) — the single-shot reading that crowned flash rank-1 was one draw from a spread as wide as the field it beat. Where the variance lives is the actionable finding: all five independent repeats found the key's structural findings (8/8 Class B sites in every output, 4/5 perfect Class A reachability, zero false Class-C alarms), and the spread collapses to 5 points (36–41) once citation-address penalties are removed — the instrument's noise is line-number fidelity, not reasoning quality, which argues for a mechanical citation-verification pass in the harness rather than more grader effort. Caveats: the noise floor is measured for the anchor lane only (the qwen lane is in flight overnight); cross-model noise is assumed, not measured; and the T447-rep cells (opus/sonnet/haiku) were graded by a different grader, so their gaps carry grader variance on top of model variance.
